results.caption: Running with the one and only @Conner Leavitt !!! 🕺⭐️🪄💨
results.profileBio:
On a mission to get the world moving.
Interviewer & Storyteller 
Host | Running Interview Show & @postrunhigh 
KateM@millentertainment.com
results.transcript: Hey Connor, how many miles are we running today? I hear the Central Park Loop is six. That cool with you? Well, I had it maybe seven weeks ago, so how about four miles? Let's do it. My name is Connor Levitt, formerly known as Mr. Whitney. Originally from Atlanta, but right now we're in New York City. I love you! I'm in Masquerade right now. Masquerade! You know the pole girl on top? Yes! That's you! Let me start my Strava run. Start! Are you a runner? I am very much into endurance sports. I don't think many people know this. I did a half Ironman in St. George, Utah. When did you do this? 2024, I believe. This run is unlocking a whole new side of Connor's brand. Yes. You were a finance bro, right? I was, yes. Just like Whitney, I have a Bachelor of Arts. So I did economics and mathematics in school and went straight into FinTech, then went on to work at Facebook, and then I got into a hedge fund. My watch is like, you're going fast! Nine Minute Miles. She's unstoppable! I'm trying to keep up with her. I'm like, oh my God! You're good at dancing. You're good at performing. You crushed it on Dancing with the Stars when you were in the dance with Whitney. Do you have any sort of performance background? Zero. I was born with two left feet. Whitney deserves all the credit for my dancing capabilities. That's just kind of how it happened. I mean, I'm not a great dancer, but my wife's an incredible teacher. I'm constantly surrounded by people who are better than me at everything. Now we're friends with people like Mark Ballas, and it pushes me. When you have people like Whitney and Mark teaching you how to dance, you're going to learn how to dance. You don't have to be a quick learner. You just have to be a willing learner. I like this pace. About a year ago, Whitney was on the Running Interview Show. Did you tell her that you were doing this today? Yes, I did. She said, you're going to have so much fun. She's like, just put in the work. Get the miles in. You and Whitney are going to be in season five of Mormon Wives. Yes. But you guys aren't returning. What was that decision like for you? It was a hard decision to make. We've grown to have real relationships with these people. To say goodbye is a hard thing to do. And you guys are starting a production company? So we started a production company so that we can start creating our own scripted stories. What types of scripted stories can we expect to see? We have a- couple of ideas. I'm gonna tell you what I will consider my passion project. You've heard of the Titanic. Of course. It was a ship that sank in 1912. They sent out a distress signal. There was only one ship that responded. The Carpathia. And the captain of the Carpathia said, may the devil himself fear the heat coming from our boilers because our sister ship is in need of aid. From that quote I go, that right there is a movie. Do you feel like when you first started out on the Mormon Wives show and eventually left your job, did it take you a little bit of time to find who Connor wanted to be? Yes. I've always been a yes guy. I never really say no. So it did take me a minute just go like, what do I want? What kind of just kind of kept resurfacing was storytelling. We're going up Cat Hill. You told me this cat was special. What the? Magic cat? We're at three miles. How are you feeling? I'm feeling it. I'm feeling it too. This is beautiful. Great place to catch the breath. I'm on mile 3.15. Let's break this up. Guys, this is the longest I've ran since having a baby. No one works harder than moms. Okay, Connor, I ask everybody this. What is the quo or motto that you live by? If you're going to do something, do it right. Have a good attitude. We're at 3.9. How are you feeling? Ready to finish strong, baby. I feel like I just ran a marathon. Four miles. Connor, who do you challenge to run with me next? Wait me. This fall, you're back up.
